final_loop_finding: first configuration in the whole project to clear the risk-adjusted gate on genuinely out-of-sample data, but it does NOT beat buy-and-hold
signal_basis: rank IC study (no strategy, no parameters): lb=250/h=20 cross-sectional momentum gives IC +0.0174, t=+2.93, stable across pre-2024 (+0.0287) and 2024+ (+0.0210) at only 12.6x annual turnover
method: walk-forward: (lookback, direction, hold) re-selected every ~3 months from a 20-config grid scored ONLY on trailing data; exposure fixed once at 4% per name as a risk-budget decision

beta_comparison_same_span.verdict: strategy did NOT beat the market. It matched beta's Sharpe while cutting drawdown from -19.5% to -12.3%, i.e. it is a lower-risk version of beta, not alpha.

control_random_universe.verdict: a real but modest selection effect, not a dominant edge

why: the only metric that clearly beats the market is drawdown, not return
on untouched data the CAGR lands at 5.99% against a 6.00% hurdle, inside the noise of a 140-trade sample
outperforming the market was the stated goal and this does not do that
a 4.3 year walk-forward over a period when beta returned 18.55% is not evidence of a durable edge
what_is_genuinely_useful: the information-coefficient framework is the durable artefact. It located a statistically significant, turnover-efficient signal (IC +0.0174 at 12.6x turnover) that every strategy-level test in this project had missed or mis-measured.
